title: The Roman School commonly rejects this: God gives being to every act of the creature immediately
source_text: IV. Verum ista opinio communiter in Schola Romana rejicitur. Paucissimis enim exceptis, consentiunt Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae tum Veteres tum recentiores, Deum ita cooperari causis secundis ut nulla sit actio causae secundae quae proxime non procedat a Deo sicut & a causa secunda, & nullam actionem posse a creatura exerceri, nisi Deus cum creatura conferat Esse illi actioni, & quidem per se & immediate.
pass_a_gloss: But that opinion is commonly rejected in the Roman School. For with very few excepted, the Doctors of the Roman Church both Old and more recent agree, that God so cooperates with second causes that there is no action of a second cause which does not proceed proximately from God as well as from the second cause, and that no action can be exercised by a creature, unless God together with the creature confer Being on that action, and that by himself and immediately.
pass_b_english: The Roman School, however, generally rejects this view. With very few exceptions, the teachers of the Roman Church, old and recent alike, agree that God cooperates with secondary causes in such a way that every action of a secondary cause comes proximately from God as well as from that cause.
No action can be performed by a creature unless God, together with the creature, gives that action its being, and does so of himself and directly.

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
